gaps.sentence: It's hard to ___ friends when you move to a new city.
gaps.explanation: make friends is the fixed expression for forming friendships.

gaps.sentence: We should ___ an effort to arrive on time.
gaps.explanation: make an effort is the fixed collocation meaning to try hard.

gaps.sentence: Grandad's best man ___ a joke that made everyone laugh.
gaps.explanation: tell a joke is the fixed collocation; 'say a joke' is not used.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.

gaps.sentence: He was so badly ___ in the fall that he needed an operation.
gaps.explanation: badly hurt is the standard collocation meaning seriously injured.

gaps.sentence: He always ___ the truth, however unpleasant it is.
gaps.explanation: tell the truth is the fixed collocation; 'say the truth' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.
